articles.title: I tried the new Apple Health app, and it’s everything I wanted from Google Health
articles.summary: I’ve been straddling the line between Google Health and Apple Health since I bought my first wearable. I went with the Fitbit Charge HR for a few weeks before returning it for an Apple Watch Sport in 2015, and went on to wear an Apple Watch for a decade. A lot has changed, with Google acquiring Fitbit and overhauling the platform since then, culminating in the recent Google Health rebrand. I initially fell for the hype, bought a Fitbit Air , and completely switched to Google Health. Now, Apple is planning an AI overhaul of its own Health app for later this year — and it’s about to win me back.

articles.title: I wanted to love Google Photos’ AI wardrobe feature — but it’s driving me crazy
articles.summary: I don’t know about you, but I’ve long had an album in Google Photos titled “Fit Checks.” Anytime I put together a new outfit, I take a picture and add it here for future reference. So, when I learned that Google Photos was about to add a similar feature using an AI-based digital wardrobe, I was excited. The idea is simple. Google Photos scans your photos, identifies the clothes you own, and builds a digital closet from your existing photo library. You can then mix and match those clothes to create outfits, with generative AI showing you what the combinations could look like.

articles.title: Google Discover now wants you to read and see less of the actual internet
articles.summary: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing a new feature called “Dive deeper” in Google Discover. The button will give you an AI-generated overview of a topic instead of sending you to a webpage. The new experience can also surface links to related stories, community reactions, and original reporting if you want to explore further. For users, it could make Discover more convenient, but it may also mean fewer people actually open the publisher articles that appear in their feeds. Google Discover is testing a new way to make you learn more about the stories appearing in your feed, and it could mean you spend less time actually reading what your favorite websites are reporting and watching videos from the creators you like.
